title: 'Pak deployed spies to find S-400s': Military official's explosive claim on Op Sindoor
content: Pakistan deployed spies and activated sleeper cells to locate S-400 air defence systems. These efforts included satellite support and electronic warfare capabilities from other nations. The S-400 system demonstrated its long-range strike capability during Operation Sindoor. It successfully intercepted a large Pakistani aircraft over 300 kilometers away. India's air defence network has expanded with additional S-400 system deliveries.

title: Colombo draw tastes like defeat as Sri Lanka dent India's WTC final hopes
content: India let a golden chance slip in Colombo as Sri Lanka's remarkable lower-order resistance forced a draw, hurting the visitors' World Test Championship hopes. Sonal Dinusha's unbeaten 133 capped a sensational series for him, while India's flat tactics and inability to dismiss the tail after dominating the match leaves India with virtually no margin for error for the remaining WTC calendar.

title: Altman defends himself after admitting he got AI's speed wrong; blames society again
content: Days after admitting he misjudged how quickly AI would disrupt the economy, Sam Altman has pushed back at critics of his AGI timeline, saying on X that his capability predictions were "actually quite good". The OpenAI chief blames society and the economy for absorbing the technology slowly, not the technology itself. His defence follows a cover story in which Mark Chen put OpenAI at 80% of the way to artificial general intelligence.

title: In 1984, Nasa sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
content: Thousands of honeybees travelled into space aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery in 1984.  These bees survived microgravity and adapted to their new environment within days.  The mission aimed to observe bee behavior and compare space-built honeycomb.  The bees successfully built approximately 200 cm of honeycomb during the seven-day mission.  Researchers noted differences in cell diameter and wall thickness compared to Earth-made structures.

title: UK households can now plug solar panels into standard sockets
content: New regulations have been established, permitting plug-in solar kits of up to 800 watts in residential settings. These systems promise substantial annual savings on electricity expenses, making renewable energy more attainable for renters and flat owners alike. Rigorous safety standards are in place to ensure secure connections, mitigating any electrical risks. This breakthrough aligns with Great Britain's rising demand for sustainable residential solar energy solutions.

title: Kyoto moves bamboo beyond visitors' reach after 350 stalks are vandalised
content: Kyoto’s famous Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is facing growing damage from tourists carving names and other writing into bamboo stalks. A city inspection found around 350 damaged plants since spring 2025. In response, Kyoto officials plan to cut about 30 sq m of bamboo as a special preservation measure and move the grove further away from the path to prevent visitors from reaching the stalks.

title: Anthropic tells employees at its San Francisco office to work from home
content: Anthropic asked its employees to work remotely this week due to a potential security guard walkout.  The security contractor, Allied Universal, had warned the AI company about this possibility.  However, the guards' union stated that no strike authorization vote has occurred.  This action by Anthropic appears to be a precautionary measure against an unconfirmed threat.  The company is preparing for a potential initial public offering soon.

title: Throat slit, dying woman writes ‘husband is my killer’ in chilling death note
content: A woman named her husband as her killer in a dying message. She was found with her throat slit outside her boutique in Pinjore. CCTV footage showed a man, suspected to be her husband, entering the shop. Police arrested the husband within two hours of the incident. The motive for the murder is currently being investigated by authorities.

title: Victor Hedman reveals why he left Lightning before Canadiens playoff games
content: Victor Hedman says that he left the Tampa Bay Lightning before the 2025-26 NHL season because of performance anxiety, physical problems and growing pressure. The veteran defenseman missed Tampa Bay’s last regular-season games and the first-round playoff series against the Montreal Canadiens. His honest explanation gives us a new glimpse into the circumstances of his absence and the mental challenges that NHL players face.

title: Travis Kelce’s $12.9m homeless donation claim exposed as fake story
content: A viral claim that Travis Kelce donated his entire $12.9 million in bonuses and endorsements to build 150 homes and 300 beds for homeless people is false. The supposed Homeless Housing Initiative could not be verified, and there was no credible evidence for the emotional quote attributed to Kelce. The Chiefs star does support charitable causes through Eighty-Seven and Running, but this specific donation story was fabricated and repeatedly resurfaced online.

title: Alex Nylander joins Flames after limited Maple Leafs opportunities in NHL
content: Alex Nylander is out of the Toronto Maple Leafs organization after two seasons and will join the Calgary Flames’ training camp on a pro tryout. The 28-year-old forward enjoyed a good campaign with the Toronto Marlies, helping to capture the Calder Cup. The NHL opportunity could be another way for Nylander to reach an NHL roster spot.

title: 'Learn Marathi in 1 year': Maharashtra govt extends deadline for auto, taxi drivers
content: Maharashtra's chief minister has taken a progressive step by implementing a one-year learning phase for drivers amid recent enforcement and protests. This initiative will offer drivers access to Marathi language classes and support materials, fulfilling their plea for extended educational time to improve their proficiency in Marathi for better communication.

title: WTC Points Table after IND vs SL 2nd Test: Where does Gambhir's side stand?
content: India and Sri Lanka drew the second Test in Colombo, with India winning the two-match series 1-0 after their Galle victory. India dominated the first innings but could not force a win after Sri Lanka fought back strongly in their second innings. The result leaves India fifth in the WTC standings with 68 points and a 51.52% PCT.

title: YouTuber Chhavi Varshney killed as SUV crashes into truck near Ujjain
content: A woman and her daughter died after their SUV collided with a truck.  The popular YouTuber Chhavi Varshney was among the deceased in the accident.  Three other passengers sustained serious injuries and were hospitalized for treatment.  The severe collision completely mangled the front of the SUV vehicle.  Police have initiated an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fatal crash.

title: How Andhra woman Venkata Narasamamba's India trip triggered US Green Card case
content: A US legal permanent resident faced immigration proceedings after an extended stay in India. Her prolonged absence raised questions about abandoning her residency status with the DHS. An immigration judge terminated removal proceedings, finding insufficient evidence against her. Despite this, she was detained by ICE after a scheduled check-in appointment. A federal court later granted her bail, ending her detention.

title: One year at the Bar, two years in training: What it now takes to become a judge
content: The Supreme Court reduced judicial service practice from three years to one. This change sparks debate on courtroom experience versus structured training. Former Justice Vipin Sanghi advocates for retaining the three-year practice period. Lawyers Vivek Narayan Sharma and Siddharth Sijoria believe the new framework can succeed. The discussion centers on readiness for judicial responsibilities and accessibility.

title: Telugu filmmaker Pavan Sadineni booked after alleging sexual abuse
content: Filmmaker Pavan Sadineni is currently embroiled in serious allegations, including sexual abuse and deceit. A woman lodged a complaint with Golconda Police on August 7, 2026, asserting that their relationship involved false promises of marriage and film roles. The allegations detail instances of physical assault and coerced sexual relations. Following these claims, Sadineni was apprehended and placed into judicial custody as the investigation unfolded.

title: For first time against India, Sri Lanka do the unthinkable in Colombo
content: Sri Lanka had lost 24 of their previous 27 Tests after being asked to follow on. Even more strikingly, they had lost all eight such Tests against India. But in Colombo, the hosts finally broke that run. This was only the fourth time Sri Lanka had managed to save a Test after being asked to follow on.

title: 'Saw several bodies, animals in river': Nepal flood survivors
content: Nepal is grappling with a catastrophic flood that has tragically claimed over 270 lives, leaving more than 800 individuals unaccounted for. Eyewitnesses share chilling tales of survival while facing the relentless rush of water. The floods have wreaked havoc on homes, infrastructure, and agricultural lands, disrupting communities and livelihoods. Furthermore, the disaster poses a significant challenge to the revered pilgrimage route to Kailash Mansarovar.

title: Pakistan-born ODI cricketer Asif Khan handed 15-month ban by ICC; here's why
content: Asif tested positive for a metabolite of mesterolone in a sample collected on September 8, 2025. Mesterolone is an anabolic steroid used to increase testosterone levels.

title: Sonal Dinusha becomes third Sri Lankan to achieve this feat against India
content: Dinusha was unbeaten on 98 at tea and did not have to wait long to complete his century. On the first ball of the third and final session, he flicked Mohammed Siraj towards mid-wicket for a couple of runs to reach the landmark. It was another brilliant innings from the Sri Lankan batter, who continued his sublime run in the two-match Test series against India.

title: ‘Living in jail at home for 6 yrs, no social life, no job’: Hathras rape victim’s family

The Allahabad High Court ordered their relocation to Noida or Ghaziabad within three months.  This move offers hope for better job opportunities and education for the family.  The family cherishes a Tulsi plant planted by the victim as a last memory.

title: Blackbeard hypersonic missile: When speed meets cheap & scalable
content: Hypersonic weapons offer speed advantages, making targets harder to intercept effectively.  However, recent conflicts highlight the need for affordable and scalable weapon systems.  Expensive systems deplete stockpiles, forcing riskier combat methods.  New developments aim to create affordable hypersonic missiles for widespread use.  Future weapons must balance speed, precision, and survivability with cost-effectiveness.

title: MBAs bag higher salaries than engineers: Top B-schools average Rs 27.4 lakh
